requirements.heading: The Format and DelSp Parameters
requirements.text: A Format value of Flowed indicates that the definition of flowed text (as specified in this memo) was used on generation, and MAY be used on reception.

requirements.heading: The Format and DelSp Parameters
requirements.text: When creating messages, DelSp SHOULD NOT be specified in Text content types other than Text/Plain with Format = Flowed.

requirements.heading: The Format and DelSp Parameters
requirements.text: When receiving messages, DelSp SHOULD be ignored if used in a Text content type other than Text/Plain with Format = Flowed.

requirements.heading: Interpreting Format=Flowed
requirements.text: A series of one or more flowed lines followed by one fixed line is considered a paragraph, and MAY be flowed (wrapped and unwrapped) as appropriate on display and in the construction of new messages (see Section 4.5).

requirements.heading: Interpreting Format=Flowed
requirements.text: An interpreting agent SHOULD allow for three exceptions to the rule that paragraphs end with a fixed line.

requirements.heading: Interpreting Format=Flowed
requirements.text: These exceptions are improperly constructed messages: a flowed line SHOULD be considered to end the paragraph if it is followed by a line of a different quote depth (see 4.5) or by a signature separator (see 4.3); the end of the body also ends the paragraph.

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: When generating Format=Flowed text, lines SHOULD be 78 characters or shorter, including any trailing white space and also including any space added as part of stuffing (see Section 4.4).

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: When this technique is used, the DelSp parameter SHOULD be used; if used it MUST be set to "no".

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: When this technique is used, the DelSp parameter MUST be used and MUST be set to "yes".

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: It is RECOMMENDED that agents avoid this by inserting the SP CRLF sequence following the existing SP.

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: Generating agents MAY use either method within each Text/Plain body part.

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: Regardless of which technique is used, a generating agent SHOULD NOT insert a space in an unnatural location, such as into a word (a sequence of printable characters, not containing spaces, in a language/coded character set in which spaces are common).

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: If faced with such a word which exceeds 78 characters (but less than 998 characters, the [SMTP] limit on line length), the agent SHOULD send the word as is and exceed the 78-character limit on line length.

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: A generating agent SHOULD:

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: In order to create messages which do not require space-stuffing, and are thus more aesthetically pleasing when viewed as Format=Fixed, a generating agent MAY avoid wrapping immediately before ">", "From ", or space.

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: When placing soft line breaks in a paragraph, generating agents MUST NOT place them in a way that causes any line of the paragraph to be a signature separator line, because paragraphs cannot contain signature separator lines (see Sections 4.3 and 6).

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: [Quoted-Printable] encoding SHOULD NOT be used with Format=Flowed unless absolutely necessary (for example, non-US-ASCII (8-bit) characters over a strictly 7-bit transport such as unextended [SMTP]).

requirements.heading: Generating Format=Flowed
requirements.text: In particular, a message SHOULD NOT be encoded in Quoted- Printable for the sole purpose of protecting the trailing space on flowed lines unless the body part is cryptographically signed or encrypted (see Section 4.6).

requirements.heading: Usenet Signature Convention
requirements.text: Generating agents MUST NOT end a paragraph with such a signature line.

requirements.heading: Space-Stuffing
requirements.text: On generation, any unquoted lines which start with ">", and any lines which start with a space or "From " MUST be space-stuffed.

requirements.heading: Space-Stuffing
requirements.text: Other lines MAY be space-stuffed as desired.

requirements.heading: Quoting
requirements.text: All lines of a paragraph MUST be unquoted, or else they MUST all be quoted and have the same quote depth.

requirements.heading: Quoting
requirements.text: Therefore, whenever there is a change in quote depth, or a change from quoted to unquoted, or change from unquoted to quoted, the line immediately preceding the change MUST NOT be a flowed line.

requirements.heading: Quoting
requirements.text: If a receiving agent wishes to reformat flowed quoted lines (joining and/or wrapping them) on display or when generating new messages, the lines SHOULD be de-quoted, reformatted, and then re-quoted.

requirements.heading: Quoting
requirements.text: The receiver SHOULD handle this error by using the 'quote-depth-wins' rule, which is to consider the paragraph to end with the flowed line immediately preceding the change in quote depth.

requirements.heading: Quoting
requirements.text: In other words, whenever two adjacent lines have different quote depths, senders MUST ensure that the earlier line is not flowed (does not end in a space), and receivers finding a flowed line there SHOULD treat it as the last line of a paragraph.

requirements.heading: Quoting
requirements.text: A generating agent MUST NOT create this situation; a receiving agent SHOULD handle it by giving preference to the quote depth.

requirements.heading: Interoperability
requirements.text: If some lines begin with one or more spaces, the generating agent MAY space-stuff all lines, to maintain the relative indentation of the lines when viewed by clients which are not aware of Format=Flowed.

requirements.heading: Interoperability
requirements.text: Thus, when generating text in languages/coded character sets in which spaces are common, the generating agent MAY always use the DelSp=no method.

requirements.heading: Interoperability
requirements.text: Hand-aligned text, such as ASCII tables or art, source code, etc., SHOULD be sent as fixed, not flowed lines.

requirements.heading: ABNF
requirements.text: flowed-body = *( paragraph / fixed-line / sig-sep ) paragraph = 1*flowed-line fixed-line ; all lines in paragraph MUST be unquoted or ; have same quote depth flowed-line = ( flowed-line-qt / flowed-line-unqt ) flow CRLF flowed-line-qt = quote ( ( stuffing stuffed-flowed ) / unstuffed-flowed ) flowed-line-unqt = ( stuffing stuffed-flowed ) / unstuffed-flowed stuffed-flowed = *text-char unstuffed-flowed = non-sp-quote *text-char fixed-line = fixed-line-qt / fixed-line-unqt fixed-line-qt = quote ( ( stuffing stuffed-fixed ) /
